Multiple Class II recalls in Neuromodulation and Direxion microcatheters have increased the risk of added cost, regulatory friction and product disruption. These issues come on top of existing pressures in PFA, WATCHMAN volumes and integration risk related to large deals and restructuring.

The SIMPLAAFY data for the WATCHMAN FLX Pro LAAC device is particularly important at the moment because it relates directly to one of Boston Scientific's weaker lines. Trial results showed that aspirin alone or reduced dose NOAC regimens achieved noninferiority to dual antiplatelet therapy at six months, with similar ischemic stroke rates and less bleeding, while device related thrombus was lowest on reduced dose NOAC.

sum: Boston Scientific lowered its near-term growth outlook after third-quarter sales increased only 1.5 percent from a year earlier. In its October 28 release, the medical technology company said revenue reached 5.138 billion US dollars in the three months ended September 30, 2026.

GAAP net income attributable to common shareholders fell to 582 million US dollars, or 0.40 US dollars per share, from 755 million US dollars, or 0.51 US dollars, a year earlier. Adjusted earnings per share declined to 0.73 US dollars from 0.75 US dollars. The company said the year had been challenging, while Chief Executive Mike Mahoney pointed to the response to a cybersecurity incident and the longer-term innovation pipeline.

Boston Scientific reported 0.7 percent organic growth in MedSurg and 1.9 percent organic growth in Cardiovascular. Within MedSurg, neuromodulation sales increased 13.0 percent on an operational and organic basis, but endoscopy sales declined 0.6 percent and urology sales fell 3.1 percent on the same basis.

Regional performance was mixed. Operational sales increased 6.1 percent in Europe, the Middle East and Africa and 10.5 percent in Latin America and Canada, while Asia-Pacific declined 1.1 percent. U.S. operational sales rose 0.5 percent.

Management expects fourth-quarter reported and organic sales to decline between 1.0 percent and 3.0 percent from the prior-year period. Adjusted earnings per share are forecast at 0.77 to 0.79 US dollars. For the full year, the company now expects reported sales growth of approximately 4.25 percent, organic growth of approximately 3.75 percent and adjusted earnings per share of 3.16 to 3.18 US dollars.

The outlook puts execution and demand trends ahead of the November 11 investor conference on the market agenda. Boston Scientific is scheduled to participate in Stifel's 2026 Healthcare Conference, where senior executives are expected to discuss the business and its product strategy.

The company started enrollment in the Elite AF trial for the next-generation WATCHMAN Elite device. It also received United States Food and Drug Administration 510(k) clearance for technologies in its StoneSmart kidney-stone treatment ecosystem and for an expanded size range of the SEISMIQ peripheral lithotripsy catheter.

Boston Scientific (BSX) stock lost 56.8% in the year to November 3, 2026, marking the worst return in a peer group of six health care companies that includes Medtronic and Stryker. The stock now trades at the lowest price to earnings in that group. Yet over its latest four quarters, Boston Scientific ranks third of six for both revenue growth and operating margin. How much less are you paying for Boston Scientific than for a rival with about the same record over the past four quarters?

Buyers pay 18.0 times earnings for Boston Scientific stock, against 32.8 times for Stryker. That works out to a little over half the price for each dollar of profit. Both companies report on the same four fiscal quarters, ended September 30, 2026. Over that period, Boston Scientific grew revenue 8.9%, setting a faster pace than Stryker’s 7.9%. Stryker posted an operating margin of 21.8%, only a little wider than Boston Scientific’s 20.6%.

Two peers grew faster than Boston Scientific. Medtronic trades at a higher multiple of 24.2 times earnings on 9.8% growth. Becton Dickinson grew 17.4%, but a financial loss in one of its latest four quarters leaves it out of the price-to-earnings ranking. Medtronic’s operating margin, though, sat at 19.0%, below Boston Scientific’s.
Boston Scientific’s Sales Growth Has Slowed For Four Quarters

Beneath that four-quarter figure, Boston Scientific’s growth slowed in every quarter. Revenue grew 15.9% from a year earlier in fiscal Q4 2025 and 11.6% in fiscal Q1 2026. Growth then dropped to 7.5% in fiscal Q2 and 1.4% in fiscal Q3 2026. Management estimates that third-quarter growth was about 3 percentage points lower because of a cyber incident. The incident left the company unable to make or ship products for eight business days.

Management says the pressure on sales comes mainly from two businesses, EP and WATCHMAN. EP sales fell 5% in the third quarter. Management says the company’s strong market share in EP has eroded as rivals introduced new technologies. WATCHMAN sales fell 7% in the U.S. The rest of the company makes up about 75% of the business and is growing consistently, management says, with its interventional cardiology business growing 19%.

Much of any recovery in Boston Scientific (BSX) stock rests on its businesses outside WATCHMAN and electrophysiology, which management expects to keep growing. The stock’s highest close of the past three years, $108.14 on September 8, 2025, is 143% above its latest close. When management cut its 2026 outlook in July 2026, the reduction was concentrated in those two businesses. Yet they are not the whole company. So how much of Boston Scientific is still growing?

On its July 29, 2026 call, management said the business units outside electrophysiology and WATCHMAN make up roughly 75% of revenue. They are expected to grow about 6% in the second half of 2026. Management said that pace matches how those units have grown for many quarters, so the slowdown has not reached them yet.

Interventional Cardiology is the standout. The unit grew 15% in the second quarter, driven by double-digit growth in coronary therapies. As the company enters new high-growth markets over the coming years, management expects Interventional Cardiology, along with the wider Interventional Cardiology and Vascular Therapies unit it belongs to, to be its strongest growth driver. Neuromodulation grew 12% in the same quarter.
Urology is the exception. Second-quarter growth came in at 1%, falling short of management’s expectations. Management now expects full-year growth for the unit to be flat to low-single digits.

So far it is, even as WATCHMAN and electrophysiology weaken. Management said the U.S. market for WATCHMAN slowed sharply and unexpectedly. It expects global WATCHMAN sales to decline mid- to high-single digits in the second half of 2026, with electrophysiology growth remaining flat. On the same call, management said WATCHMAN is less than 10% of revenue.

In the second quarter of 2026 alone, Boston Scientific’s operating margin was 22.9%, up from 18.6% a year earlier. Over the twelve months to June 30, 2026, the margin was 21.0%, up from 18.3%. That is the highest it has been at any quarter end in the past ten years.

sum: Boston Scientific stock closed at USD 42.98 on the NYSE on September 11, 2026, down 0.28% from the prior session, before pre-market trading on September 14, 2026 pointed to a modest rebound in the wake of a significant cyberattack disclosure.

According to Yahoo Finance on September 13, 2026, Boston Scientific Corporation reported that an August 25, 2026 cyberattack disrupted manufacturing and shipping and is expected to have a material impact on its third-quarter and full-year 2026 net sales and adjusted earnings per share guidance.

The company stated that, based on currently available information, it is unlikely to meet its previously issued guidance for net sales growth and adjusted EPS in 2026, which had been communicated in late July 2026, and that the cyber incident will weigh on results despite operations having resumed.

As Security Measures Lab reported on September 14, 2026, Boston Scientific detailed in a Form 8-K filed with the SEC on September 8, 2026 that the incident is likely to significantly affect its results for the third quarter and full year 2026, prompting the company to warn that its previously communicated guidance for 2026 sales growth and adjusted EPS may not be achieved.

Despite the guidance downgrade, Boston Scientific emphasized that core operations have returned to normal, with manufacturing, order processing and product shipments fully restored by September 9, 2026, roughly two weeks after the August 25, 2026 incident, according to Security Measures Lab.

The same report notes that Boston Scientific and external cybersecurity experts such as CrowdStrike found no evidence of compromise in product technology or several key systems, and the company currently does not expect the cyberattack to have a major long-term impact on its financial position, even though the short-term hit to 2026 earnings is assessed as significant.

The attack also led to a temporary halt and subsequent resumption of remote monitoring enablement for cardiac device communicators and insertable cardiac monitors, a sensitive area for patients and physicians that Boston Scientific addressed once the technical problem was resolved, as outlined by Security Measures Lab.

Third, the gap between the initial August 25 disclosure and the September 8 financial warning highlights how difficult the ultimate impact was to quantify. sum: Boston Scientific (NYSE: BSX), the medical device maker, said on Tuesday it no longer expects to meet its 2026 sales and profit guidance after a cyberattack disrupted operations worldwide.

BSX shares were down 2.1% in premarket trading, according to Reuters, building on a longer decline that has seen the stock more than halve from its 52-week high of $108.07. The shares closed at $47.80 on Friday, near their 52-week low of $42.20.

Boston Scientific said it first identified unauthorised activity on some of its IT systems on 25 August, which caused a global network outage that cut off access to operating systems and business applications. The outage disrupted manufacturing and the processing and shipment of customer orders across the company’s global operations, the company said.

As a result, Boston Scientific said it is unlikely to hit the Q3 and full-year 2026 sales and adjusted-profit guidance it issued on 29 July, which had called for full-year adjusted earnings per share of $3.28 to $3.32 and reported net sales growth of 5.5% to 6.5%. The company said it has made progress restoring systems, with major distribution centres now processing and shipping at or above normal levels and manufacturing resumed across most facilities globally, and it expects to recover a portion of the lost revenue as operations ramp back up.

The incident adds Boston Scientific to a run of cyberattacks that have hit healthcare companies this year. The company has not yet quantified the financial hit and said it will give an updated outlook when it reports Q3 earnings on 28 October.
